dimensions.assessment: Directly affects covered entities receiving federal financial assistance under the CHIPS Act and equipment manufacturers.
dimensions.evidence: each agreement with a covered entity for the award of Federal financial assistance under section 9902

dimensions.assessment: Places strict 10-year prohibitions on procuring specified equipment from foreign entities of concern, directly altering project sourcing and procurement options.
dimensions.evidence: prohibitions with respect to a project relating to the procurement, installation, or use of ineligible semiconductor manufacturing equipment

dimensions.assessment: Applies restrictions to existing federal financial assistance awarded under the CHIPS Act, potentially shifting commercial purchasing costs without specifying new appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: agreement with a covered entity for the award of Federal financial assistance under section 9902

dimensions.assessment: Amends specific sections of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 by adding definitions and funding restrictions.
dimensions.evidence: Section 9901 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (15 U.S.C. 4651) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Mandates that prohibitions remain in effect for a duration of 10 years beginning on the date the agreement is signed.
dimensions.evidence: to be effective for 10 years beginning on the date on which the agreement is signed.

missing_information: The exact number of covered entities or total dollar volume of affected contracts is not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: The Chip EQUIP Act amends the CHIPS Act provisions to prohibit companies receiving federal CHIPS funding from purchasing specified foreign-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment for 10 years, impacting federally funded project supply chains and participating manufacturers.
